title: Network Analyzer
summary: A Bash-driven wireless security learning environment with a local browser interface for authorized network observation and lab-based Wi-Fi assessment.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.title: Learning wireless security by observing a controlled lab.
paragraphs: Network Analyzer packages common wireless-analysis tools behind a guided Bash workflow and a lightweight local web interface. The repository explicitly describes the project as educational and discourages unauthorized activity.

sections.label: Tooling
sections.title: A Linux-oriented shell and browser workflow.
points: Checks for root privileges and supported Linux distributions
Uses Bash for the interactive analysis workflow
Serves the accompanying interface through a restricted Python HTTP server
Keeps example output and learning resources alongside the source

sections.label: Scope
sections.title: Capabilities belong inside an authorized environment.
paragraphs: The repository describes traffic observation, wireless discovery, handshake capture, client deauthentication, and password-auditing exercises. Those operations can interrupt networks and must be limited to isolated labs or networks with explicit written permission.
sections.callout: Use only hardware and networks you own or have explicit authorization to test.

sections.label: Implementation
sections.title: Transparent components that can be inspected before use.
paragraphs: The public repository includes the main Bash workflow, a Python static server, browser-side JavaScript, interface assets, process notes, and selected upstream source references. This makes the learning environment inspectable before privileged execution.

architecture.title: Network Analyzer execution model
architecture.summary: A privileged Bash workflow coordinates wireless utilities while a small Python server exposes local interface and learning assets in the browser.
steps: mybash.sh verifies root access, detects the Linux distribution, and checks for required Aircrack-ng and mdk utilities.
The shell workflow presents guided network-analysis options and invokes installed command-line tools against a selected wireless interface.
server.py uses Python's standard HTTP server on port 8000 and restricts translated paths to the current working directory.
HTML, CSS, and browser-side JavaScript provide the local visual interface and supporting process information.
Captured material and audit exercises must stay inside an isolated, authorized lab; the web interface does not remove the safety implications of privileged wireless operations.

validation.title: Network Analyzer authorized-lab checklist
validation.summary: Safe static, interface, dependency, and lab-scope checks for a tool whose privileged wireless operations require explicit authorization.
checks: Run bash -n mybash.sh and python3 -m py_compile server.py before executing either component.
Start server.py as an unprivileged user and confirm the interface loads locally while path traversal remains blocked.
Review the supported-distribution detection and verify every required wireless utility comes from a trusted package source.
Document the access point, adapter, channel, client devices, written authorization, and time window for the isolated lab.
Confirm the workflow refuses non-root privileged operations and clearly displays the educational-use warning.
After the exercise, stop monitor mode, restore network services, remove captures securely, and record outcomes without third-party identifiers.

pageNote: This page combines the project overview, architecture, usage, validation, safety boundaries, status, and source links in one case study.
